steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: An AND gate outputs 1 only when ALL inputs are 1; its truth table has one high output for two inputs.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: An OR gate outputs 1 when ANY input is 1; it produces a low output only when all inputs are 0.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A NOT gate (inverter) outputs the complement of its single input: 0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A NAND gate is the complement of AND: output is 0 only when all inputs are 1; it is a universal gate.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Draw the truth table for a 2-input AND gate. | Q: What is the output of a NAND gate when both inputs are 1? | Q: Why are NAND and NOR called universal gates?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A=0,B=0→0; A=0,B=1→0; A=1,B=0→0; A=1,B=1→1. | 0. A NAND gate produces the complement of the AND output. | Because any Boolean function can be implemented using only NAND gates or only NOR gates, without needing any other gate type.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always write truth tables with inputs in binary counting order (00, 01, 10, 11). Remember: NAND = NOT(AND); NOR = NOT(OR); the bubble on the symbol indicates inversion. When asked to identify a gate from a truth table, look at which rows give output 1. For universal gate questions, show how NOT, AND and OR can each be made from NAND gates. Label gate symbols clearly with the gate type and input/output labels.
